## Purpose

Widen the exploration beyond the pre-specified contrasts (analysis/06) with
five families of contrasts, each modelled according to the audits. All results
here are hypothesis-generating.

| Family | Contrasts | Model |
|---|---|---|
| F1 lung histology | neuroendocrine vs non-small cell; adenocarcinoma vs squamous | `~ batch + group` |
| F2 lung genotypes | KRAS, SMARCA4, KRAS vs EGFR | `~ batch + histology + co-mutations + group` (D28) |
| F3 KRAS subsets | STK11 (KL), TP53 (KP), CDKN2A (KC) within KRAS-mutant lung lines | `~ batch + histology + co-mutation + group` |
| F4 tissue vs rest | each tissue with >= 5 lines vs all other lines | `~ batch + group` |
| F5 screens within tissues | each gene of Dataset EV4 (and MTAP) in lung, breast and bladder | `~ batch + (histology) + TP53 + gene` |

**Decision supported:** which contrasts to carry forward to enrichment
(Phase 5) and to the final selection.

## Inputs

- `data/derived/cancer-cell-lines/shorthouse_v1/shorthouse_analysis_v1.rds`
- `data/raw/cancer-cell-lines/msb202211006-sup-0005-datasetev4.xlsx` (genes tested by Shorthouse et al.)
- `config.yml`: `contrast` (gene roles), `exploratory`

## Methods

Status follows the gene roles (D19, D25, D27, D29), and lung contrasts are
blocked by histology (D28). The KRAS subsets follow Skoulidis F et al.
(*Cancer Discov* 2015. doi:10.1158/2159-8290.cd-14-1236, PMID 26069186),
who describe three subsets of KRAS-mutant lung adenocarcinoma "dominated,
respectively, by co-occurring genetic events in STK11/LKB1 (the KL subgroup),
TP53 (KP), and CDKN2A/B inactivation". Each subset is compared with the other
KRAS-mutant lung lines. A contrast is fitted only if both groups have at least
`min_per_group` lines (approved exploratory minimum). Models are fitted with
limma on all 1096 ions, BH within each contrast.

**Guard against imputed values** (audit/09): with small groups, one line at the
half-minimum floor can make an ion significant. For each ion, the number of the
contrast's lines with an imputed value is counted. The summary reports
significant ions both in total and among ions without any imputed value in the
contrast's lines ("robust").

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/use_case.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/plotting.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/mutations.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/differential.R"))
config <- load_config()
derived_dir <- uc_dir(config, "derived")
raw_dir <- uc_dir(config, "raw")
output_dir <- uc_dir(config, "output", "07_exploratory_contrasts")

data <- readRDS(file.path(derived_dir, "shorthouse_analysis_v1.rds"))
params <- config$exploratory
models <- filter(data$lines, in_models)
```

```{r helpers}
# fit one contrast if both groups are large enough; returns summary row and result table
run_contrast <- function(id, family, d, terms) {
    n_altered <- sum(d$group)
    n_unaltered <- sum(!d$group)
    row <- tibble(family = family, contrast = id, altered = n_altered, unaltered = n_unaltered)
    if (min(n_altered, n_unaltered) < params$min_per_group) {
        return(list(summary = mutate(row, status = "too few lines"), table = NULL))
    }
    X <- tryCatch(contrast_design(d, terms), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(X)) return(list(summary = mutate(row, status = "not estimable"), table = NULL))
    tab <- fit_contrast(data, d, X)$table %>%
        mutate(family = family, contrast = id, imputed_lines = imputed_altered + imputed_unaltered)
    row <- row %>% mutate(
        status = "fitted",
        terms = paste(setdiff(colnames(X), "(Intercept)"), collapse = " + "),
        residual_df = nrow(X) - ncol(X),
        adj_p_below_0.05 = sum(tab$adj.P.Val < 0.05),
        robust_adj_p_below_0.05 = sum(tab$adj.P.Val < 0.05 & tab$imputed_lines == 0),
        min_adj_p = min(tab$adj.P.Val),
        null_share = round(limma::propTrueNull(tab$P.Value), 2)
    )
    list(summary = row, table = tab)
}
```

## 1. Declared contrasts (F1–F3)

```{r declared}
declared <- lapply(names(params$contrasts), function(id) {
    spec <- params$contrasts[[id]]
    run_contrast(id, spec$family, exploratory_lines(data, spec, config), c(spec$blocking, spec$covariates))
})
bind_rows(lapply(declared, `[[`, "summary")) %>%
    preview_table(caption = "Declared contrasts")
```

KRAS vs EGFR is not fitted under the current oncogene rule (D29): only two
lung lines count as EGFR-altered.

## 2. Tissue vs rest (F4)

```{r tissue-vs-rest}
tissues <- models %>% count(tissue) %>% filter(n >= params$tissue_vs_rest$min_lines) %>% pull(tissue)
tissue_results <- lapply(tissues, function(t) {
    d <- tissue_vs_rest_lines(data, t)
    run_contrast(paste0(tolower(t), "_vs_rest"), "F4 tissue vs rest", d, character())
})
bind_rows(lapply(tissue_results, `[[`, "summary")) %>%
    preview_table(caption = "Tissue vs rest")
```

## 3. Screens within tissues (F5)

```{r screens}
ev4 <- readxl::read_excel(file.path(raw_dir, "msb202211006-sup-0005-datasetev4.xlsx"), sheet = "Sheet1", n_max = 1)
candidates <- union(sub("^T_", "", setdiff(names(ev4), "ionIdx")), "MTAP")

screen_results <- list()
for (t in params$tissue_screens$tissues) {
    base <- models %>% filter(tissue == t) %>% select(line, tissue, batch, histology)
    # genes with enough altered and unaltered lines in this tissue
    status <- sapply(candidates, function(g) altered_status(data, base$line, g, config))
    n_altered <- colSums(status, na.rm = TRUE)
    n_known <- colSums(!is.na(status))
    genes <- candidates[n_altered >= params$min_per_group & n_known - n_altered >= params$min_per_group]
    blocking <- if (t == "Lung") "histology" else character()
    for (g in genes) {
        covs <- setdiff(params$tissue_screens$covariates, g)
        d <- base
        d$group <- status[, g]
        for (cov in covs) d[[cov]] <- altered_status(data, d$line, cov, config)
        d <- filter(d, !is.na(group), if_all(all_of(covs), ~ !is.na(.x)))
        screen_results[[paste(t, g)]] <- run_contrast(paste0(tolower(t), "_", g), paste("F5 screen", t), d,
                                                      c(blocking, covs))
    }
}
screen_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(screen_results, `[[`, "summary"))
screen_summary %>% count(family, status)
screen_summary %>%
    filter(status == "fitted") %>%
    arrange(desc(robust_adj_p_below_0.05), min_adj_p) %>%
    preview_table(caption = "Screens within tissues")
```

Lines in the altered group of the screens with at most five altered lines,
and how many genes each line carries mutations in. In small groups, the
results of genes mutated in the same few lines are not independent.

```{r small-groups}
mutated_genes <- data$mutation_status %>% count(line, name = "mutated_genes")
small <- screen_summary %>% filter(status == "fitted", altered <= 5)
# altered lines per small screen
altered_lines <- bind_rows(lapply(names(screen_results), function(k) {
    tissue <- sub(" .*", "", k); gene <- sub(".* ", "", k)
    base <- models %>% filter(tissue == !!tissue)
    s <- altered_status(data, base$line, gene, config)
    tibble(contrast = paste0(tolower(tissue), "_", gene), line = names(s)[s %in% TRUE])
})) %>%
    filter(contrast %in% small$contrast) %>%
    left_join(mutated_genes, by = "line")
altered_lines %>%
    group_by(line, mutated_genes) %>%
    summarise(small_screens = n(),
              screens_with_hits = sum(contrast %in% small$contrast[small$robust_adj_p_below_0.05 > 0]),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(desc(screens_with_hits)) %>%
    preview_table(caption = "Lines in the altered groups of small screens")
# for comparison: median number of mutated genes per line
median(mutated_genes$mutated_genes[mutated_genes$line %in% models$line])
```

## 4. Overview

```{r overview}
all_results <- c(declared, tissue_results, screen_results)
summary_all <- bind_rows(lapply(all_results, `[[`, "summary"))
tables <- bind_rows(lapply(all_results, `[[`, "table"))
readr::write_tsv(summary_all, file.path(output_dir, "exploratory_summary.tsv"))
readr::write_tsv(tables, file.path(output_dir, "exploratory_results.tsv"))

summary_all %>%
    group_by(family) %>%
    summarise(fitted = sum(status == "fitted"), skipped = sum(status != "fitted"),
              with_robust_hits = sum(robust_adj_p_below_0.05 > 0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r overview-plot, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 7}
families <- sort(unique(summary_all$family))
p <- summary_all %>%
    filter(status == "fitted", adj_p_below_0.05 > 0) %>%
    ggplot(aes(robust_adj_p_below_0.05, reorder(contrast, robust_adj_p_below_0.05), fill = family)) +
    geom_col() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = uc_palette(families)) +
    labs(x = "Ions with adjusted p < 0.05 (no imputed values)", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
         title = "Exploratory contrasts with significant ions") +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "overview", output_dir, width = 9, height = 7)
p
```

Significant ions without imputed values:

```{r hits}
tables %>%
    filter(adj.P.Val < 0.05, imputed_lines == 0) %>%
    arrange(family, contrast, P.Value) %>%
    transmute(family, contrast, feature_id, name = substr(name, 1, 60), logFC = round(logFC, 2),
              adj.P.Val = signif(adj.P.Val, 2)) %>%
    preview_table(caption = "Robust significant ions")
```

## Interpretation

"Robust" below means adjusted p < 0.05 and no imputed value among the
contrast's lines.

- **F1 lung histology:** neuroendocrine vs non-small cell lines is the
  strongest exploratory contrast (14/69, 55 robust ions, estimated share of
  null ions 0.78). The leading ions include cystathionine (log2FC +2.9),
  S-adenosylhomocysteine, purine nucleotides (dADP, IMP) and several
  phospholipids, all higher in neuroendocrine lines. Adenocarcinoma vs
  squamous shows nothing (39/15).
- **F2 lung genotypes:** KRAS in lung (blocked by histology, adjusted for
  TP53, STK11 and KEAP1) has no signal. SMARCA4 in lung has 2 robust ions.
  KRAS vs EGFR was not fitted (two EGFR lines under D29).
- **F3 KRAS subsets:** no subset (KL 8/17, KP 19/6, KC 12/10) has a
  significant ion. With 25 KRAS-mutant lines the subsets are small.
- **F4 tissue vs rest:** colon (19 robust ions), kidney (13) and skin (10;
  smallest adjusted p 10⁻²⁰) differ from the other lines. Lung (3), blood (1),
  bladder, breast, ovary and pancreas (0) hardly do once batch is in the model.
- **F5 screens within tissues:** among the 19 screens with more than five
  lines per group, only KEAP1 in lung (8 robust ions, the same ions as the
  NRF2 control) and MUC16 in lung (5) have hits. MUC16 is a long gene with
  many passenger variants (analysis/03). Screens with at most five altered
  lines produce hits in 20 of 57 cases, but the same few highly mutated lines
  recur in their altered groups. NCIH2342 (1666 mutated genes vs a median of
  356) is in 7 small screens, 6 of them with hits; NCIH1155 (1420) in 7, with
  hits in 4. These hits describe single lines rather than genes and are not
  interpretable at the gene level.

**Overall:** beyond the NRF2/KEAP1 signal, the clearest metabolic differences
are between lineages: neuroendocrine vs non-small cell lung lines, and
colon, kidney and skin vs the rest. Genotype contrasts other than NRF2 show
little at the ion level. These contrasts are candidates for the
enrichment analysis (Phase 5), which may pick up coordinated weak changes.
